## Goal

A self-hostable remote server that serves many homes safely on a separate user-content domain, signs viewers in, lets an operating layer enforce its limits through ports, and gives cloud chat hosts a remote MCP server, so inline artifacts persist there.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

the public server on WP-29's core (ARCHITECTURE §15, D165):
- viewer sign-in: identity providers behind their port (OpenID Connect and GitHub adapters), account viewers with verified names, anonymous viewers per browser, and the full authorization server (Client ID Metadata Documents, Dynamic Client Registration, PKCE, resource indicators, `iss`, rotating refresh tokens);
- the hosted shell's rules and its trusted chrome (D161), the report control, and policy hooks for interstitials and expiry (HY-09);
- the operator ports (`limits`, `metering`, `accounts`, `abuse`, `policy`, `routing`, `events`, and `invitations` reserved) with no-op defaults, the server handle, and hostnames an operator supplies;
- anonymous answers at D165 item 13's targets with per-IP and per-link limits (RM-08);
- pause and resume from the CLI and the operator (RM-09);
- the remote MCP endpoint on `@mostra/mcp`'s factory, with authoring relayed to the default owner instance, so WP-17's MCP Apps persist in cloud chat hosts;
- a container image and self-hosting docs;
- the adversarial suite of D159 and D165.

Design detail for this package:

- WP-28 designed this package's surface (D165, M56): ARCHITECTURE §15, INTERFACES §18, DATA_MODEL §7 and FAILURE_MODEL §11. Build them as written; settle finer shapes under D123 and record each additively in those sections, and bring Mirza any place where the design is wrong or silent.
- From WP-15 (D164): serve `@mostra/mcp`'s `createMcpServerFactory` with the remote server's own ports (WP-28's design) behind OAuth: the SDK's `createMcpHandler` takes `fetch(request, { authInfo })`, and tool handlers read nothing else of the transport. `onClient` reports each client's `clientInfo`, which D148 names as where usage of the plugin route is measured. The `mcp-tools` wire-schema bundle and `server.test.ts`'s check that `tools/list` serves exactly it hold the schemas ChatGPT freezes (D32): a remote tool of its own joins the bundle.
- From WP-14 (D162): turn on the harness plugin's remote MCP server: `features.remoteMcp` in `tools/plugins/definition.ts` with `enabled: true`, the production `url` and the service's `privacyPolicyUrl` (Anthropic's directory asks a plugin with a remote server for one); the generator adds it to every manifest and the README, and the check holds both to `https:`. OpenAI's directory takes a local MCP server only from allowlisted partners, so this server, with OAuth and no plan display or upgrade prompt (D147; the plugin check refuses such words), is the plugin's MCP route there, and the route for surfaces that install no local plugin: ChatGPT and OpenAI's dots (account-installed plugins), Grok Bot (cloud skills and connectors) and Meta's Muse app (a reviewed connector). Record each surface's submission steps with Mirza (VERIFIED_FACTS, WP-14). In Anthropic's directory, WP-14's listing (submitted from `mostra-dev/mostra-plugin`, 2026-10-31) is listed on Claude Code only, because the Skill needs a local shell and a browser on the same machine: once the release carrying the remote server is published, tick **Cowork** and **Claude apps** on the plugin's **Settings** tab in the developer portal (claude.ai/directory/manage; no new submission), and submit the remote server as an **MCP connector** linked to the plugin (Anthropic's docs: a plugin that references a remote server you run submits it as a connector too), with OAuth, the privacy policy and a reviewer test account. Both need Mirza's sign-in; the portal's controls don't take an automated browser's clicks.
- Sign-in (INTERFACES §18.5): identity providers behind their port, with OpenID Connect and GitHub adapters configured in `identityProviders`; accounts separate from their identities; viewers of kind `account` (names verified by their provider) and `anonymous` (one per browser, names unverified); the full authorization server: Client ID Metadata Documents advertised with `none` among the token endpoint's methods (Claude uses one only then), Dynamic Client Registration, PKCE S256, resource indicators with an audience check, `iss` in responses, rotating refresh tokens with `offline_access`, every endpoint within 10 s. Enterprise identity (SAML, SCIM) plugs into the same port and isn't built here (D165 item 11).
- The hosted shell's rules (ARCHITECTURE §15.6), each with a check red on a seed: the apex serves only the shell; every hosted response sends `Origin-Agent-Cluster: ?1` and the shell never sets `document.domain`; no credential is bound to the user-content domain (no passwords, no WebAuthn whose relying-party ID is the domain or a name under it), and sign-in happens only on the API origin; the shell's resources send `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`, and no check treats `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site` as trust; framing `'none'` (D145). Then D161's chrome (the sender line, "Never enter passwords", generic previews, `noindex`, the after-submit line), the report control and `policy`'s interstitial and expiry (HY-09).
- Cookie-free sessions (D165 item 8): seed a cookie tossed onto the parent domain, a cookie named to shadow a session, and a sibling page filling the jar past 180 cookies; each leaves every hosted session working (HY-08).
- Operator ports (INTERFACES §18.6): `limits`, `metering`, `accounts` (with a first sign-in step and operator-issued credentials), `abuse` (reports, the after-push hook, the server handle's actions), `policy`, `routing` (hostnames an operator supplies; decide where the shell sits for an outside domain within the shell's rules, and prove an unknown `Host` gets nothing), `events` (at least once, stable IDs) and `invitations` (reserved for WP-31, no mailer), each with its time limit and no-op default, proved with a fixture operator module. Their types are exported by `@mostra/protocol` (`@mostra/protocol/operator`), so an operating layer imports nothing else of Mostra; the managed service's layer consumes the published packages only.
- Anonymous answers (RM-08, D165 item 13): a load test against the container image with the owner offline at 1 a second for 30 minutes and bursts of 10 a second, p95 acceptance under 0.5 s; per-IP and per-link limits answering 429 with the shell's "try again shortly", nothing dropped; `once` per anonymous browser, recorded unverified.
- Pause (RM-09, D165 item 14): `mostra pause` and `resume`, `artifact/pause`, and the operator handle's pause, which the owner can't undo.
- The remote MCP endpoint (INTERFACES §18.8): reading tools on the account's hosted home, authoring through the default owner instance (`port/relay.author`), `MOSTRA_REMOTE_NO_INSTANCE` without one, and `artifact_open` returning the hosted link. `@mostra/runtime`'s `server` module may import `@mostra/mcp` for it (REPO_STANDARDS §3).
- Check boundary for MC-04 (D125 puts this package before WP-17): prove the endpoint, its authorization and an agent in a cloud chat host creating, opening (through the hosted link) and submitting an artifact. The MCP App exporter, its client transport and the app-only tools are WP-17's; WP-17 repeats the check inline through this server. Build nothing WP-17 would have to work around: the app-only tools of INTERFACES §12 are served by the same handlers.
- The container image (D165 item 11): multi-architecture Linux, a non-root user, one data volume, configuration from environment variables or a file, published by the release pipeline with the other artifacts (D36); self-hosting docs with a Caddy front and a wildcard certificate; one small machine runs RM-08's page.
- The adversarial suite (D159, D165), each a seeded negative test: cross-home reads and writes, tokens in logs, `Referer` headers and URLs, cookie tossing, origin isolation, relay replay and flood, OAuth redirect abuse and quota bypass. RM-03's audit shows no operating-layer code in the core: the open server contains no implementation of plans, quotas, billing, abuse scoring, placement, backup automation, domain moves, webhooks or mail (D165 item 11).

## Out of scope

- The managed service's operating layer: accounts beyond sign-in, billing, quotas, metering storage, abuse tooling, placement, backup automation and fleet operation (outside this repository, D116, D165 item 11)
- `ee/` features: SAML, SCIM, audit log, retention and organization policies, an admin console (D118)
- Sandboxed remote execution (RM-06, v1.x)
- Team features beyond the reserved surface (WP-31)

## Risks and notes

- ChatGPT's write tools on a custom MCP server need a Business or Enterprise workspace, and approved tool snapshots freeze (VERIFIED_FACTS, WP-28): arrange the external check with Mirza early, and keep schemas additive (D32).
- Cross-tenant isolation is hygiene: seeded cross-tenant reads, writes and frame entries are negative tests, as WP-05's are.
- A public-suffix entry for the user-content domain can't be counted on (D137): every check runs without one.

## Handoff

Hosted links on a real remote server, and inline Mostra that persists in cloud chat hosts; WP-31 builds team features on its viewer identity.
